system.docHtml:
The caster lays hands upon a quantity of base material — raw iron ore, rough-hewn stone, even salvaged scrap — and channels transformative energy through it. The material's composition shifts at the fundamental level, impurities separating and burning away, crystalline structures realigning into the dense, regular patterns of high-quality steel. The transformation is visible: dull gray ore brightens to a steel-blue sheen, rough surfaces smooth as the material densifies, and the characteristic ring of quality metal sounds when the product is struck.

The transmuted steel is genuine in every respect — it can be worked, tempered, and alloyed exactly as naturally produced steel would be. The spell's primary value lies in logistics: an army's worth of quality steel can be produced from common iron in a fraction of the time conventional smelting requires, and in locations far from any forge. The quantity of material that can be transmuted in a single casting depends on the caster's power, ranging from enough for a knife blade at novice level to a full suit of armor's worth at mastery.
